name: New Caledonia
summary: French civil law applies, so children have a protected share (the réserve) that a will cannot cut. People with Kanak customary status follow custom on customary land. A foreign resident cannot choose their national law, and the EU Succession Regulation does not apply. The Hague Trusts Convention is not in force for France.
reserved_share: Children: 1/2 with one child, 2/3 with two, 3/4 with three or more (Code civil art 913); if no descendants, a surviving spouse 1/4 (art 914-1). Applies outside customary land and to persons under common-law civil status.
foreign_law_note: The EU Succession Regulation does not apply in New Caledonia (an overseas country and territory). Under French common-law conflict rules, land follows the law of its location and movables the last domicile, so a resident cannot select national law (not verified from a New Caledonia source).
trust_note: The fiducie (Code civil arts 2011 ff.) is a statutory trust with narrow uses; its extension to New Caledonia was not verified. Foreign trusts: France has signed but not ratified the Convention. Foundations: only charitable forms (fondations, fonds de dotation) are known in France; local availability not verified.
open_questions: Whether fiducie and fondation law extend to New Caledonia (civil law was transferred to the territory in 2013).
Whether Code civil arts 912-914 apply unchanged locally.
The 2021 compensatory-levy rule (art 913) in this territory.
